:::info

Die Dokumentation dieser Integration wird von ihrem Autor geschrieben und ist bisher nur auf Englisch verfügbar.

:::

Bring your [Strava](https://www.strava.com) activities into Gladys: sensors
with your latest activity and your weekly, monthly and yearly distances, scene
triggers when you finish an activity or beat a personal record, and two
dashboard widgets.

Requires Gladys 5.1 or later and a Strava account (a free account is enough).

## 1. Create your Strava API application

Strava gives each user their own API application: the integration uses yours,
so your data only travels between Strava and your Gladys.

1. Sign in on strava.com and open
   [Settings → My API Application](https://www.strava.com/settings/api).
2. Fill in the form:
   - **Application Name**: for example `Gladys`;
   - **Category**: `Other`;
   - **Website**: the address of your Gladys, or `https://gladysassistant.com`;
   - **Authorization Callback Domain**: the **host name** you type in your
     browser to open Gladys, without `http://`, port or path — for example
     `192.168.1.20` or `gladys.local`. If you open Gladys through Gladys Plus,
     use the host name of that address instead. `localhost` is always
     accepted by Strava.
3. Upload any icon if Strava asks for one, then save.
4. Keep the page open: you need the **Client ID** and the **Client Secret**.

## 2. Configure the integration

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations → Strava → Configuration**.
2. Paste the **Client ID** and the **Client Secret**, then **save**.
3. Click **Connect** next to "Strava account": Strava asks you to authorize
   the application. **Keep every permission ticked** (the private activities
   one too, or your private activities are left out), then confirm.
4. Back in Gladys, the status turns to "connected" and a **Strava** device
   appears in the **Discovery** tab: add it to get its sensors.

Options:

- **Units**: metric (km, m, km/h) or imperial (mi, ft, mph). Changing it
  updates the device definition: accept the update offered in the Discovery
  tab.
- **Refresh interval**: how often Strava is read, every 15 minutes by default
  (5 minutes minimum, Strava limits the number of requests).
- **Weekly distance goal**: all sports together, in km (or miles). Used by the
  "Strava weekly goal reached" trigger and the dashboard widget; 0 disables it.

## 3. Instant notifications with Gladys Plus (optional)

Without Gladys Plus, a new activity shows up at the next refresh. With Gladys
Plus, paste your Gladys Plus **Open API key** in the "Gladys Plus webhooks"
block of the Configuration screen: the integration then registers a Strava
webhook, and Strava announces each new activity within seconds.

Strava allows one webhook per API application: use a dedicated application
for each Gladys.

## The Strava device

| Sensor                                  | Unit               |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| Last activity (name) / sport            | text               |
| Last activity distance                  | km or mi           |
| Last activity moving time               | minutes            |
| Last activity elevation gain            | m or ft            |
| Last activity average speed             | km/h or mph        |
| Distance / moving time this week        | km or mi / minutes |
| Run, ride, swim distances, last 4 weeks | km or mi           |
| Run, ride, swim distances this year     | km or mi           |

The week starts on Monday, in the time zone of your latest activity. The 4
weeks and year totals are Strava's own: they only count run, ride and swim
activities, and only the activities visible to everyone.

## Scenes

The integration adds its own cards to the scene editor, under the
**Integrations** category.

Triggers:

- **New Strava activity** — an activity was recorded or uploaded. Optionally
  filter on the sport (run, ride, swim, walk or hike, other). The following
  actions can use `{{triggerEvent.data.name}}`, `sport`, `sport_type`,
  `distance`, `distance_unit`, `moving_time` (minutes), `elevation_gain`,
  `average_speed`, `pr_count`, `activity_id` and `url`.
- **Strava personal record** — a new activity beat at least one of your
  records (`name`, `sport`, `pr_count`, `url`...).
- **Strava weekly goal reached** — the distance of the week reached your goal,
  once a week (`week_distance`, `goal`, `week_activities`).

Each activity is announced once, even after a restart; the activities that
existed before the account was linked are not announced.

Actions:

- **Synchronize Strava** — reads Strava now; returns `new_activities`.
- **Get Strava statistics** — distance, moving time, elevation gain and count
  of a period (this week, last 4 weeks, this year, all time) for one sport or
  all, to use in a message: "\{\{...distance\}\} \{\{...distance_unit\}\} this week!".
- **Get the last Strava activity** — name, sport, distance, time and link of
  your latest activity.

Every action also returns `linked`: false when no account is linked, so a
scene can check it instead of failing.

Example: "When a new run is recorded, send me a Telegram message with its
distance, and flash the living room light if it was a personal record".

## Dashboard

- **Strava this week**: distance, moving time, number of activities and
  elevation of the week, a 7-day distance chart, your weekly goal, the last
  activity and your yearly run and ride distances. **Sync now** refreshes
  right away, **Open Strava** opens your profile.
- **Strava activities**: your latest activities (3, 5 or 8, optionally one
  sport only); tap one for the details and a link to Strava.

## Actions of the Configuration screen

- **Test the connection** — reads Strava and shows who is connected and the
  activities of the week.
- **Synchronize now** — refreshes everything right away.
- **Unlink the Strava account** — revokes the access on Strava and forgets the
  tokens. Click **Connect** to link an account again.

## Troubleshooting

- **"redirect_uri invalid" on the Strava page**: the Authorization Callback
  Domain of your Strava application does not match the address you use to
  open Gladys. Set it to that host name (step 1).
- **The status says Strava refused the access**: the access was revoked on
  strava.com or the application changed. Click **Connect** again.
- **The badge of the device shows an orange dot**: the Strava request limit
  was reached; the next refresh catches up. Increase the refresh interval if
  it happens often.
- Check the integration logs from the Gladys UI (or `docker logs` on the
  host); start the container with `LOG_LEVEL=debug` for the full detail.

You can revoke the access of the integration at any time from
[strava.com/settings/apps](https://www.strava.com/settings/apps).

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt Strava in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create your Strava API application | `section` | Nein | On strava.com, open Settings > My API Application and create an application. As "Authorization Callback Domain", enter the host name you use to reach Gladys (\{\{gladys_host\}\}). Then copy its Client ID and Client Secret below, save, and click Connect. |
| Client ID | `string` | Ja |  |
| Client Secret | `secret` | Ja |  |
| Strava account | `oauth2` | Nein | Save the Client ID and Client Secret first, then link your Strava account. Keep every permission ticked on the Strava page. |
| Preferences | `section` | Nein | Optional: with Gladys Plus, paste your Open API key in the "Gladys Plus webhooks" block to get your new activities within seconds instead of at the next refresh. |
| Units | `select` | Nein |  |
| Refresh interval (min) | `number` | Nein | How often Strava is read, in minutes (5 to 240). |
| Weekly distance goal | `number` | Nein | In km (or miles in imperial units), all sports together. 0 disables the goal. |

## So installierst du Strava in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Strava erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/quentinlegay/gladys-strava:1.0.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/quentinlegay/gladys-strava](https://github.com/quentinlegay/gladys-strava).

Strava benötigt Gladys `>=5.1.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Strava ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [quentinlegay](https://github.com/quentinlegay) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
